description: The bookkeeping that stops the checklist becoming a survey. These gates answer to the run's own state rather than to an attestation, so the run cannot close by claiming it is finished.

gates.title: The Run Was Opened Before The Work
gates.rule: A run exists and the changes are recorded against it. Work done outside a run is work nothing checked, and an unchecked change looks exactly like a passing one afterwards.

gates.title: Scope Is Every Route, Not The One Named
gates.rule: The targets cover every route a crawler reaches, not only the page the prompt mentioned. A title fixed on one route and left wrong on nine others has not been fixed.
gates.fix: Widen the targets with scan --target, or answer n/a naming why those routes are outside this deliverable.

gates.title: Every File In Scope Was Read And Ruled On
gates.rule: Each file under the targets ends either changed or explicitly ruled as needing no SEO change, with the reason. A file nobody opened and a file considered and left alone are indistinguishable without this.
gates.fix: seo-pass.py files, then read each one and either change it or file-clear it with a note.

gates.title: Copy A Person Reads Passes The Writing Standard
gates.rule: Titles, descriptions and body copy are read by people before they are parsed by a crawler, so they answer to the avoid-ai-writing standard like any other user-facing string.
gates.fix: Invoke avoid-ai-writing and rewrite what it flags, then verify again.

gates.title: Every Applicable Gate Is Answered
gates.rule: No gate is left silent. A gate that is not met is work to do; the only ways past one are changing the project or naming the condition that puts it out of scope.
gates.fix: seo-pass.py status lists what is open.

gates.title: The Filled Checklist Was Rendered
gates.rule: The run ends with the whole checklist shown - every gate, its verdict, the evidence, and a section listing anything answered not applicable and why.
